chunks: And by this chain, he said, Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
A family will never be poor that uses vinegar and oil for their sauce, and that is the sauce of the Prophets (peace be upon them).
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of vinegar and oil in Shia tradition regarding poverty and prophetic lifestyle?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies vinegar and oil as the 'condiment of the Prophets,' linking this simple dietary practice to spiritual humility and divine sustenance. In Shia tradition, this hadith underscores the virtue of simplicity (zuhd) and serves as a practical reminder that reliance on God is maintained through modest means rather than material excess. The reference to 'those who seek sustenance' (ya'tadimuna) highlights the active, daily engagement with these basic provisions as a form of gratitude.
